title: Orbital Mechanics / Astronautics
description: This syllabus treats orbital mechanics as an applied astronautics course: students move from two-body motion and orbit elements to maneuvers, rendezvous, interplanetary trajectories, perturbations, re-entry, and spacecraft mission design.

topics.title: Astronautics Context, Space Mission Architecture, and Space Environment
topics.description: Introduce astronautics as the engineering of spacecraft missions, orbital regimes, and the space operating environment.

children.title: Mission Architecture
children.description: Students learn how orbital mechanics fits into the broader design of a space mission.

children.title: Mission objective, payload, spacecraft bus, launch vehicle, ground segment, and operations concept
LEO, MEO, GEO, HEO, cislunar, heliocentric, and interplanetary mission classes
Science, communication, navigation, Earth observation, crewed, defense, and technology demonstration missions
Requirements, constraints, interfaces, margins, and mission phases
Space Environment
children.description: The point is to understand the environment that shapes orbit choice and spacecraft design.

children.title: Vacuum, microgravity, plasma, atomic oxygen, radiation belts, solar wind, and micrometeoroids
Thermal cycling, eclipse, sunlight, albedo, and Earth infrared radiation
Space weather, solar activity, geomagnetic storms, and single-event effects
Debris environment, conjunction risk, and space situational awareness
Spacecraft System Overview
children.description: This subtopic gives students a working vocabulary for spacecraft constraints.

children.title: Structure, power, thermal control, propulsion, attitude control, communications, avionics, and payload
Mass budget, power budget, link budget, propellant budget, and thermal balance
Reliability, redundancy, fault protection, and autonomy
Launch loads, vibration, deployment, commissioning, and end-of-life disposal

topics.title: Coordinate Systems, Time Systems, and Reference Frames
topics.description: Define the frames, time scales, and geometry used to describe spacecraft position and velocity.

children.title: Reference Frames
children.description: Students need frames before they can describe position, velocity, and attitude correctly.

children.title: Inertial frame, Earth-centered inertial frame, Earth-centered Earth-fixed frame, and perifocal frame
Topocentric horizon frame, local vertical/local horizontal frame, and body frame
Right ascension, declination, latitude, longitude, altitude, azimuth, and elevation
Frame transformation, rotation matrix, direction cosine matrix, and quaternion preview
Time Systems and Earth Orientation
children.description: Time definitions matter because orbit prediction is a time-sensitive geometric calculation.

children.title: UTC, TAI, TT, UT1, Julian date, sidereal time, and leap second
Greenwich sidereal time, local sidereal time, and Earth rotation angle
Precession, nutation, polar motion, and Earth orientation parameters as advanced context
Epoch, time of periapsis passage, and propagation interval
Vector Geometry for Orbits
children.description: The goal is to make orbital equations geometrically meaningful.

children.title: Position vector, velocity vector, acceleration vector, angular momentum vector, and eccentricity vector
Specific mechanical energy, node vector, line of apsides, and orbital plane
Dot product, cross product, projection, and vector norm
Right-handed coordinate system and sign convention

topics.title: Two-Body Problem and Equations of Orbital Motion
topics.description: Derive and interpret the ideal gravitational two-body model underlying most orbital mechanics.

children.title: Newtonian Gravity and Relative Motion
children.description: This subtopic develops the ideal model behind Keplerian orbits.

children.title: Newton's law of gravitation, gravitational parameter, reduced mass, and relative position
Equation of relative motion and inverse-square central force
Point mass assumption, spherical body assumption, and isolated two-body approximation
Acceleration due to gravity and standard gravitational parameter mu
Conservation Laws
children.description: Students learn why ideal orbits are conic sections with constant orbital properties.

children.title: Specific angular momentum, conservation of angular momentum, and orbital plane
Specific mechanical energy, bound orbit, escape condition, and hyperbolic excess velocity
Eccentricity vector, Laplace-Runge-Lenz vector, and line of apsides
Circular, elliptical, parabolic, and hyperbolic conics
Conic Orbit Geometry
children.description: The point is to connect equations to orbit shape and mission behavior.

children.title: Semi-major axis, semi-latus rectum, eccentricity, periapsis, apoapsis, and radius equation
True anomaly, flight-path angle, and orbital speed
Vis-viva equation and circular speed
Escape velocity and characteristic energy C3

topics.title: Classical Orbital Elements and State Vector Conversion
topics.description: Represent orbits using six classical elements and convert between elements and position-velocity vectors.

children.title: Classical Orbital Elements
children.description: Students learn the standard six numbers used to define a Keplerian orbit.

children.title: Semi-major axis, eccentricity, inclination, right ascension of ascending node, argument of periapsis, and true anomaly
Ascending node, descending node, periapsis direction, and orbital plane orientation
Special cases: circular orbit, equatorial orbit, and singular elements
Mean anomaly and epoch as alternate element components
State Vector to Elements
children.description: This subtopic turns position and velocity into orbit geometry.

children.title: Specific angular momentum vector, node vector, eccentricity vector, and energy
Inclination from angular momentum, RAAN from node vector, and argument of periapsis from geometry
Quadrant checks, atan2 usage, and numerical tolerances
Handling circular, equatorial, parabolic, and hyperbolic edge cases
Elements to State Vector
children.description: The goal is to generate position and velocity from orbital elements.

children.title: Perifocal coordinates, p-q-w frame, and conic radius
Perifocal velocity, flight-path geometry, and rotation sequence
Rotation by RAAN, inclination, and argument of periapsis
State vector validation using energy, angular momentum, and vis-viva

topics.title: Kepler's Laws, Anomalies, and Orbit Propagation
topics.description: Use Keplerian motion to predict spacecraft position as a function of time.

children.title: Kepler's Laws and Periodic Motion
children.description: Students learn how orbit size and timing are linked.

children.title: Kepler's first, second, and third laws
Orbital period, mean motion, areal velocity, and time since periapsis
Circular orbit speed, elliptical period, and semi-major-axis dependence
Limits of Keplerian propagation
Anomalies and Kepler's Equation
children.description: This subtopic gives the machinery for finding spacecraft position at a given time.

children.title: True anomaly, eccentric anomaly, mean anomaly, and mean motion
Kepler's equation for elliptical orbits
Newton iteration for Kepler's equation and convergence concerns
Hyperbolic anomaly and hyperbolic Kepler equation
Orbit Propagation
children.description: The point is to predict future state under ideal two-body assumptions.

children.title: Time of flight, propagation from epoch, and anomaly update
Lagrange f and g functions as an alternate propagation method
Universal variables, Stumpff functions, and conic-independent propagation preview
Propagation error and need for perturbation models

topics.title: Ground Tracks, Visibility, and Orbit Design
topics.description: Analyze how orbital geometry affects coverage, revisit, communication windows, and ground station access.

children.title: Orbital Regimes and Mission Fit
children.description: Students connect orbit choices to mission objectives.

children.title: Low Earth orbit, medium Earth orbit, geostationary orbit, geosynchronous orbit, highly elliptical orbit, and cislunar orbit
Polar orbit, sun-synchronous orbit, frozen orbit, Molniya orbit, and repeat ground-track orbit
Altitude, inclination, eccentricity, period, coverage, revisit, and radiation environment
Earth observation, communications, navigation, reconnaissance, and science missions
Ground Tracks and Access
children.description: This subtopic shows how orbital motion appears from Earth.

children.title: Ground track, subsatellite point, nodal regression, and Earth rotation
Visibility cone, elevation mask, horizon, pass duration, and contact window
Ground station, line of sight, footprint, and swath width
Revisit time, coverage gap, and constellation coverage
Orbit Design Trade-Offs
children.description: The goal is to compare orbit choices with mission constraints.

children.title: Launch site latitude, inclination access, delta-v cost, and range safety
Resolution, coverage, latency, power, thermal, drag, and communications constraints
Constellation spacing, phasing, plane count, and Walker constellation preview
End-of-life disposal and debris mitigation

topics.title: Orbit Determination, Tracking, and Navigation
topics.description: Estimate spacecraft state from observations and understand navigation uncertainty.

children.title: Tracking Measurements
children.description: Students learn what observations can tell us about spacecraft state.

children.title: Range, range rate, Doppler, angles-only tracking, right ascension, declination, azimuth, and elevation
Ground station geometry, measurement noise, bias, and time tag
Two-line element, radar tracking, optical tracking, and GNSS receiver data
Observation residual and measurement model
Initial Orbit Determination
children.description: This subtopic introduces how an orbit can be inferred from limited observations.

children.title: Gauss method, Gibbs method, Lambert problem, and angles-only problem as named methods
Line-of-sight vector, observation arc, and preliminary orbit
Three-position vector method and velocity estimation
Ambiguity, observability, and geometry strength
Estimation and Navigation Uncertainty
children.description: The point is to treat orbit knowledge as uncertain and updateable.

children.title: Least squares, weighted least squares, state estimate, covariance, and residual
Extended Kalman filter, process noise, measurement noise, and prediction/update cycle
Orbit determination accuracy, dilution of precision, and covariance propagation
Autonomous navigation and ground-based navigation trade-offs

topics.title: Impulsive Orbital Maneuvers and Delta-V Budgeting
topics.description: Analyze velocity changes for orbit raising, lowering, phasing, inclination changes, and mission budgets.

children.title: Impulsive Maneuver Basics
children.description: Students learn how instantaneous velocity changes alter orbits.

children.title: Delta-v vector, prograde burn, retrograde burn, radial burn, and normal burn
Periapsis burn, apoapsis burn, impulsive approximation, and finite-burn limitation
Vis-viva equation for pre/post maneuver speed
Orbit raising, orbit lowering, circularization, and deorbit burn
Delta-V and Propellant
children.description: This subtopic connects orbital mechanics to propulsion sizing.

children.title: Total delta-v budget, maneuver margin, gravity loss, drag loss, and finite-burn loss
Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, specific impulse, effective exhaust velocity, and mass ratio
Dry mass, wet mass, propellant mass, and payload fraction
Chemical propulsion, electric propulsion, thrust level, and burn duration
Maneuver Planning
children.description: The goal is to plan sequences rather than isolated burns.

children.title: Maneuver node, burn timing, burn direction, and target orbit
Apse line rotation, inclination correction, argument-of-periapsis adjustment, and phasing
Combined maneuver and split maneuver trade-offs
Operational constraints: ground contact, eclipse, thermal, plume, and collision avoidance

topics.title: Hohmann Transfers, Plane Changes, and Rendezvous
topics.description: Study common transfer strategies and the geometry of meeting another spacecraft.

children.title: Hohmann and Bi-Elliptic Transfers
children.description: Students learn the standard energy-efficient transfer patterns between circular orbits.

children.title: Hohmann transfer, transfer ellipse, perigee burn, apogee burn, and circularization
Transfer time, transfer semi-major axis, and total delta-v
Bi-elliptic transfer, intermediate apoapsis, and when it can help
LEO-to-GEO transfer, GTO, and apogee kick motor context
Plane Changes and Combined Maneuvers
children.description: This subtopic covers costly geometry changes in orbital planes.

children.title: Inclination change, node line, normal burn, and plane-change angle
Plane-change delta-v and dependence on speed
Combined plane change with speed change
Best location for plane change and apogee advantage
Rendezvous Phasing
children.description: The point is to arrive at the same place at the same time.

children.title: Phasing orbit, phase angle, synodic period, and catch-up time
Lead angle, chase vehicle, target vehicle, and transfer window
Coelliptic rendezvous, terminal phase, and closing rate
ISS rendezvous, docking corridor, and safety constraints

topics.title: Relative Motion and Proximity Operations
topics.description: Model nearby spacecraft motion for docking, inspection, formation flying, and safety zones.

children.title: Relative Motion Frames
children.description: Students learn how nearby spacecraft motion is described from the target spacecraft.

children.title: Local vertical/local horizontal frame, radial/in-track/cross-track directions, and Hill frame
Relative position, relative velocity, line of sight, and range rate
Target orbit, chaser orbit, and relative orbital elements
Keep-out sphere, approach corridor, and passive safety
Hill-Clohessy-Wiltshire Equations
children.description: This subtopic introduces the classic linear model for nearby circular-orbit motion.

children.title: Linearized relative motion, mean motion, radial equation, along-track equation, and cross-track equation
Natural relative motion, drift, bounded motion, and periodic relative orbit
Impulse response and relative maneuver planning
Assumptions: circular reference orbit, small separation, and two-body dynamics
Proximity Operations and Formation Flying
children.description: The goal is to connect relative motion to mission operations.

children.title: Rendezvous, docking, berthing, inspection, servicing, and formation flying
Approach ellipsoid, collision avoidance maneuver, and abort trajectory
Relative navigation sensors: lidar, camera, radar, and GPS
Autonomous guidance, fault detection, and operational procedures

topics.title: Interplanetary Trajectories and Patched-Conic Mission Design
topics.description: Extend two-body methods to heliocentric transfers and planetary encounters.

children.title: Patched-Conic Approximation
children.description: Students learn a tractable way to design multi-body deep-space missions.

children.title: Sphere of influence, heliocentric transfer, planet-centered hyperbola, and patch point
Departure hyperbola, arrival hyperbola, v-infinity vector, and C3
Parking orbit departure and hyperbolic escape
Capture burn, flyby, and direct entry options
Interplanetary Transfers
children.description: This subtopic extends Hohmann thinking beyond Earth orbit.

children.title: Heliocentric Hohmann transfer, synodic period, launch window, and phase angle
Time of flight, transfer angle, Lambert problem, and porkchop plot
Mars transfer, Venus transfer, outer planet transfer, and asteroid rendezvous examples
Arrival speed, entry speed, and capture delta-v
Mission Design Constraints
children.description: The goal is to balance trajectory math with spacecraft and operations constraints.

children.title: Launch vehicle capability, launch energy, declination of launch asymptote, and launch site
Power, communications, thermal environment, radiation, and planetary protection
Trajectory correction maneuver, navigation uncertainty, and deep-space tracking
Science objectives, operations timeline, and contingency margins

topics.title: Gravity Assists and Low-Energy Trajectory Concepts
topics.description: Analyze how planetary flybys reshape heliocentric energy and mission geometry.

children.title: Flyby Geometry
children.description: Students learn how a planet can redirect heliocentric velocity.

children.title: Powered flyby, unpowered flyby, v-infinity incoming, v-infinity outgoing, and turn angle
B-plane, impact parameter, periapsis radius, and flyby altitude
Planetocentric hyperbola and heliocentric velocity change
Leading-side flyby, trailing-side flyby, energy gain, and energy loss
Gravity-Assist Mission Design
children.description: This subtopic shows why flybys are central to deep-space missions.

children.title: Gravity-assist sequence, resonant flyby, pump angle, and targeting
Voyager, Galileo, Cassini, Parker Solar Probe, and Europa/outer-planet mission examples
Launch energy reduction, inclination change, and mission duration trade-off
Navigation accuracy and planetary encounter constraints
Low-Energy Trajectory Ideas
children.description: The point is to preview modern trajectory design beyond simple conics.

children.title: Restricted three-body problem, Lagrange point, invariant manifold, and weak stability boundary
Ballistic capture, lunar transfer, and cislunar trajectory
Low-thrust trajectory preview and continuous acceleration
Trade-offs among time, propellant, complexity, and navigation risk

topics.title: Orbital Perturbations, Stationkeeping, and Long-Term Evolution
topics.description: Account for non-ideal forces that change real spacecraft orbits over time.

children.title: Perturbing Forces
children.description: Students learn why real orbits depart from ideal Keplerian motion.

children.title: Earth oblateness, J2 perturbation, atmospheric drag, solar radiation pressure, third-body gravity, and thrust errors
Secular effect, periodic effect, and short-period variation
Osculating elements versus mean elements
Perturbation acceleration and numerical propagation
Common Perturbation Effects
children.description: This subtopic connects perturbations to operational orbit behavior.

children.title: Nodal regression, apsidal rotation, drag decay, eccentricity change, and inclination drift
Sun-synchronous orbit design from J2 nodal regression
Frozen orbit, repeat ground track, and atmospheric density variability
Lunar/solar perturbations for GEO, HEO, and cislunar orbits
Stationkeeping and End-of-Life
children.description: The goal is to manage orbital evolution over the mission life.

children.title: Stationkeeping box, north-south stationkeeping, east-west stationkeeping, and inclination control
Drag makeup, orbit maintenance, collision avoidance, and conjunction assessment
Deorbit, graveyard orbit, passivation, and disposal orbit
Space debris mitigation, 25-year rule context, and operational risk

topics.title: Re-Entry, Spacecraft Systems, and Integrated Mission Analysis Project
topics.description: Connect orbital mechanics to spacecraft subsystems, atmospheric entry, operations, and mission design synthesis.

children.title: Re-Entry and Entry Dynamics
children.description: Students learn the first-order mechanics of returning through an atmosphere.

children.title: Entry interface, ballistic coefficient, lift-to-drag ratio, heating rate, deceleration, and stagnation point
Ballistic entry, lifting entry, skip entry, and corridor concept
Thermal protection system, ablator, heat shield, and peak heat load
Landing ellipse, guidance, and recovery constraints
Spacecraft Systems Coupled to Orbits
children.description: This subtopic ties orbit design to spacecraft engineering.

children.title: Power generation, eclipse duration, battery sizing, and solar array pointing
Thermal control, radiator view factor, albedo, and beta angle
Communications link, antenna pointing, ground contact, and data volume
Attitude determination and control, reaction wheel, magnetorquer, thruster, and star tracker
Mission Analysis Project
children.description: The final project asks students to integrate orbital mechanics with mission constraints.

children.title: Mission objective, orbit selection, access analysis, and ground track
Maneuver plan, delta-v budget, propellant estimate, and launch constraint
Perturbation assessment, stationkeeping strategy, and disposal plan
Technical report, plots, assumptions, limitations, and design recommendation
